samples.summary: In-memory fallback stores the preference without `isFormat` validation, unlike the localStorage read path
samples.evidence: `setDateFormat` assigns `memoryFormat = format` (date-format-preference.ts:57) with no runtime check, and `getDateFormat` returns `memoryFormat` verbatim (line 50) — it only validates values that came from storage (line 42). The single caller performs an unchecked cast on a value handed in by the Select widget: `onValueChange={(value) => setDateFormat(value as DateDisplayFormat)}` (packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx:71). So an arbitrary string reaching that handler (a DOM-manipulated/injected SelectItem value, or any future caller) would be echoed back out of `getDateFormat` when storage throws, bypassing the type guard that the storage path enforces. Blast radius is cosmetic: the value only selects a formatter branch in `formatListDate` and is never interpolated into HTML, a URL, or a query — React escapes the rendered cell — so this is hardening, not an exploit. Mirroring the storage path with `memoryFormat = isFormat(format) ? format : DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` (or validating at the cast site) makes the trust boundary uniform.
